item.title: For the first time ever, Google Search is less than 50% of Alphabet's revenue (273 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://www.kadoa.com/companies/insights/google-search-below-half, See on Hacker News

29 Oct 2026

In the quarter to Sep 2026, Google Search made $63.4B of Alphabet's $128B in revenue, or 49.7%. It is the first quarter below half since Alphabet began reporting Search revenue separately. In the 31 quarters before, Search was between 52.8% and 62.0%. Over the same years, Google Cloud grew from 4.4% of revenue to 24.1%.

$63.4B

$64.2B

$30.7B

Each quarter's revenue from Google Search & other and from Google Cloud, as a share of Alphabet's total revenue. Everything else is YouTube ads, subscriptions and devices, Google Network and Other Bets.

Dec 2018 to Sep 2026

About the data

  • Search is the line Alphabet reports as "Google Search & other": ads on Google Search and on other Google properties such as Gmail, Maps and Google Play. YouTube ads, the ad network, subscriptions, devices, Google Cloud and Other Bets are counted in everything else.
  • Search revenue still grew: the share fell because the rest of Alphabet grew faster.

item.title: H.264 Is Magic (2016) (144 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://sidbala.com/h-264-is-magic/, See on Hacker News

H.264 is a video compression codec standard. It is ubiquitous - internet video, Blu-ray, phones, security cameras, drones, everything. Everything uses H.264 now.

H.264 is a remarkable piece of technology. It is the result of 30+ years of work with one single goal: To reduce the bandwidth required for transmission of full-motion video.

Technically, it is very interesting. This post will give insight into some of the details at a high level - I hope to not bore you too much with the intricacies. Also note that many of the concepts explained here apply to video compression in general, and not just H.264.

Why even compress anything?

A simple uncompressed video file will contain an array of 2D buffers containing pixel data for each frame. So it's a 3D (2 spatial dimensions and 1 temporal) array of bytes. Each pixel takes 3 bytes to store - one byte each for the three primary colors (red, green and blue).

1080p @ 60 Hz = 1920x1080x60x3 => ~370 MB/sec of raw data.

This is next to impossible to deal with. A 50GB Blu-ray disk will only hold ~2 mins. You can't move it anywhere fast. Even SSDs have trouble dumping this straight from RAM to Disk[^1].

So yeah. We need compression.

Why H.264 compression?

Yes, I will answer this. But first let me show you something. Here is the Apple Homepage:

I captured the screen of this home page and produced two files:

  • PNG screenshot of the Apple homepage 1015KB
  • 5 Second 60fps H.264 video of the same Apple homepage 175KB

Eh. What? Those file sizes look switched.

No, they're right. The H.264 video, 300 frames long is 175KB. A single frame of that video in PNG is 1015KB.

It looks like we're storing 300 times the amount of data in the video. But the file size is a fifth. So H.264 would seem to be 1500x as efficient as PNG.

How is this even possible? All right, what's the trick?

There are very many tricks! H.264 uses all the tricks you can think of (and tons you can't think of). Let's go through the important ones.

Shedding weight

Imagine you're building a car for street racing. You need to go faster. What is the first thing you do? You shed some weight. Your car weighs 3000 lbs. You throw away stuff you don't need. Those back seats? pfft. Chuck those. That subwoofer? Gone. No music for you. Air Conditioning? Yeah, ditch it. Transmission? Ye..no. Wait! We're gonna need that.

You remove everything except the things that matter.

This concept of throwing away bits you don't need to save space is called lossy compression. H.264 is a lossy codec - it throws away less important bits and only keeps the important bits.

PNG is a lossless codec. It means that nothing is thrown away. Bit for bit, the original source image can be recovered from a PNG encoded image.

Important bits? How does the algorithm know what bits in my frame are important?

There are few obvious ways to trim out images. Maybe the top right quadrant is useless all the time. So maybe we can zero out those pixels and discard that quadrant. We would use only 3/4th of the space we need. ~2200 lbs now. Or maybe we can crop out a thick border around the edges of the frame, the important stuff is in the middle anyway. Yes, you could do these. But H.264 doesn't do this.

What does H.264 actually do?

H.264, like other lossy image algorithms, discards detail information. Here is a close-up of the original compared with the image post-discard.

See how the compressed one does not show the holes in the speaker grills in the MacBook Pro? If you don't zoom in, you would even notice the difference. The image on the right weighs in at 7% the size of the original - and we haven't even compressed the image in the traditional sense. Imagine your car weighed just 200 lbs!

7% wow! How do you discard detail information like that?

For this we need a quick math lesson.

Information Entropy

Now we're getting to the juicy bits! Ha puns! If you took an information theory class, you might remember information entropy. Information entropy is the number of bits required to represent some information. Note that it is not simply the size of some dataset. It is minimum number of bits that must be used to represent all the information contained in a dataset.

For example, if your dataset is the result of a single coin toss, you need 1 bit of entropy. If you have record two coin tosses, you'll need 2 bits. Makes sense?

Suppose you have some strange coin - you've tossed it 10 times, and every time it lands on heads. How would you describe this information to someone? You wouldn't say HHHHHHHHH. You would just say "10 tosses, all heads" - bam! You've just compressed some data! Easy. I saved you hours of mindfuck lectures. This is obviously an oversimplification, but you've transformed some data into another shorter representation of the same information. You've reduced data redundancy. The information entropy in this dataset has not changed - you've just converted between representations. This type of encoder is called an entropy encoder - it's a general-purpose lossless encoder that works for any type of data.

Frequency Domain

Now that you understand information entropy, let's move on to transformations of data. You can represent data in some fundamental units. If you use binary, you have 0 and 1. If you use hex, you have 16 characters. You can easily transform between the two systems. They are essentially equivalent. So far so good? Ok!

Now, some imagination! Imagine you can transform any dataset that varies over space(or time) - something like the brightness value of an image, into a different coordinate space. So instead of x-y coordinates, let's say we have frequency coordinates. freqX and freqY are the axes now. This is called a frequency domain representation. There is another mindfuck mathematical theorem[^2] that states that you can do this for any data and you can achieve a perfect lossless transformation as long as freqX and freqY are high enough.

Okay, but what the freq are freqX and freqY?

freqX and freqY are some other set of basis units. Just like when we switch from binary to hex, we have a different fundamental unit, we're switching from the familiar X-Y to freqX and freqY. Hex 'A' looks different from binary '1010'. Both mean the same thing, but look different. So here is what our image looks like in the frequency domain:

The fine grill on that MacBook pro has a high information content in the higher frequency components of that image. Finely varying content = high frequency components. Any sort of gradual variation in the color and brightness - such as gradients are low frequency components of that image. Anything in between falls in between. So fine details = high freq. Gentle gradients = low freq. Makes sense?

In the frequency domain representation, the low frequency components are near the center of that image. The higher frequency components are towards of the edges of the image.

Okay. Kinda makes sense. But why do all this?

Because now, you can take that frequency domain image and then mask out the edges - discard information which will contain the information with high frequency components. Now if you convert back to your regular x-y coordinates, you'll find that the resulting image looks similar to the original but has lost some of the fine details. But now, the image only occupies a fraction of the space. By controlling how big your mask is, you can now tune precisely how detailed you want your output images to be.

Here is the close-up of the laptop in the home page again. Except now, there is a circular border mask that's been applied.

The numbers represent the information entropy of that image as a fraction of the original. Even at 2%, you won't notice the difference unless you're at this zoom level. 2%! - your car now weighs 60 lbs!

So that's how you shed weight. This process in lossy compression is called quantization[^3].

Okay. Impressive, I guess. What else you got?

Chroma Subsampling.

The human/eye brain system is not very good at resolving finer details in color. It can detect minor variations in brightness very easily but not color. So there must be some way to discard color information to shed even more weight.

In a TV signal, R+G+B color data gets transformed to Y+Cb+Cr. The Y is the luminance (essentially black and white brightness) and the Cb and Cr are the chrominance (color) components. RGB and YCbCr are equivalent in terms of information entropy.

Why unnecessarily complicate? RGB not good enough for you?

Back before we had color TV, we only had the Y signal. And when color TVs just started coming along, engineers had to figure out a way to transmit RGB color along with Y. Instead of using two separate data streams, they wisely decided to encode the color information into Cb and Cr and transmit that along with the Y information. That way, BW TVs would only look at the Y component. Color TVs will, in addition, look at the chrominance components and convert to RGB internally.

But check out the trick: the Y component gets encoded at full resolution. The C components only at a quarter resolution. Since the eye/brain is terrible at detecting color variations, you can get away with this. By doing this, you reduce total bandwidth by one half, with very little visual difference. Half! Your car now weighs 30 lbs!

This process of discarding some of the color information is called Chroma Subsampling[^4]. While not specific to H.264 and has been around for decades itself, it is used almost universally.

Those are the big weight shedders for lossy compression. Our frames are now tiny - since we discarded most of the detail information and half of the color information.

Wait. That's it? Can we do something more?

Yes. Weight shedding is only the first step. So far we're only looking at the spatial domains within a single frame. Now it's time to explore temporal compression - where we look at a group of frames across time.

Motion compensation

H.264 is a motion compensation compression standard.

Motion compensation? What now?

Imagine you're watching a tennis match. The camera is fixed at a certain angle. The only thing moving is the ball back and forth. How would you encode this information? You do what you always do, right? You have a 3D array of pixels, two dimensions in space and one in time. Right?

Nah. Why would you? Most of the image is the same anyway. The court, the net, the crowds, all are static. The only real action is the ball moving. What if you could just have one static image of everything in the background, and then one moving image of just the ball? Wouldn't that save a lot of space? You see where I am going with this? Get it? See where I am going? Motion estimation?

Lame jokes aside, this is exactly what H.264 does. H.264 splits up the image into macro-blocks - typically 16x16 pixel blocks that it will use for motion estimation. It encodes one static image - typically called an I-frame(Intra frame). This is a full frame - containing all the bits it required to construct that frame. And then subsequent frames are either P-frames(predicted) or B-frames(bi-directionally predicted). P-frames are frames that will encode a motion vector for each of the macro-blocks from the previous frame. So a P-frame has to be constructed by the decoder based on previous frames. It starts with the last I-frame in the video stream and then walks through every subsequent frame - adding up the motion vector deltas as it goes along until it arrives at the current frame.

B-frames are even more interesting, where the prediction happens bi-directionally, both from past frames and from future frames. So you can imagine now why that Apple home page video is so well compressed. Because it's really just three I-frames in which the macro blocks are being panned around.

Let's say you've been playing a video on YouTube. You missed the last few seconds of dialog, so you scrub back a few seconds. Have you noticed that it doesn't instantly start playing from that timecode you just selected. It pauses for a few moments and then plays. It's already buffered those frames from the network, since you just played it, so why that pause?

Yeah that annoys the shit out of me. Why does it do that?

Because you've asked the decoder to jump to some arbitrary frame, the decoder has to redo all the calculations - starting from the nearest I-frames and adding up the motion vector deltas to the frame you're on - and this is computationally expensive, and hence the brief pause. Hopefully you'll be less annoyed now, knowing it's actually doing hard work and not just sitting around just to annoy you.

Since you're only encoding motion vectors deltas, this technique is extremely space-efficient for any video with motion, at the cost of some computation.

Now we've covered both spatial and temporal compression! So far we have a shitton of space saved in Quantization. Chroma subsampling further halved the space required. On top of that, we have motion compensation that stores only 3 actual frames for the ~300 that we had in that video.

Looks pretty good to me. Now what?

Now we wrap up and seal the deal. We use a traditional lossless entropy encoder. Because why not? Let's just slap that on there for good measure.

Entropy Coder

The I-frames, after the lossy steps, contain redundant information. The motion vectors for each of the macro blocks in the P and B-frames - there are entire groups of them with the same values - since several macro blocks move by the same amount when the image pans in our test video.

An entropy encoder will take care of this redundancy. And since it is a general purpose lossless encoder, we don't have to worry about what tradeoffs it's making. We can recover all the data that goes in.

And, we're done! At the core of it, this is how video compression codecs like H.264 work. These are its tricks.

Ok great! But I am curious to know how much our car weighs now.

The original video was captured at an odd resolution of 1232x1154. If we apply the math here, we get:

5 secs @ 60 fps = 1232x1154x60x3x5 => 1.2 GB
Compressed video => 175 KB

If we apply the same ratio to our 3000 lb car, we get 0.4 lbs as the final weight. 6.5 ounces!

Yeah. It's magic!

Obviously, I am massively oversimplifying several decades of intense research in this field. If you want to know more, the Wikipedia Page is pretty descriptive.

Have comments? Did I get something wrong? Not a fan of the lame jokes? Offended by the swearing? Use HackerNews or Reddit for voicing your opinion!

Or hit me up on Twitter or LinkedIn if you want to chat.

[^1]SSD Benchmarks

[^2]Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem

[^3][Quantization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantization_(signal_processing)

[^4]Chroma Subsampling

item.title: LLM Voice (119 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/LLM-Voice.html, See on Hacker News

Sometimes when I read a post, I get the growing feeling that I'm reading the output of an LLM. I can't necessarily define why, although there are the common tells (it's not the em-dashes, it's the load-bearing tapestries). As I do this my desire to read on atrophies, sometimes to the point of revulsion

There are tools out there that claim to be able to tell the difference between LLM-written prose and the old-fashioned biological product. I'm wary of them, partly due skeptism about their accuracy, but also because it rather misses the point. The reaction to LLM-Voice is a human one, that sense that we are in an uncanny valley of prose. By the time I'd reach for a tool to tell me what I'm reading, it's already too late, even if it confidently tells me there's no LLM present.

I'm also suspicious of my own ability to accurately recognize LLM voice. Language changes over time, so a common sign of age is complaining about the language of the youngs. I'm inclined to bristle at prose that talks about “adopting a new sales motion,” or “a sharp round-up of news”. But I've heard these constructs coming out of human mouths, so that's more a generational difference rather than between carbon and silicon. (And as a transplanted Brit, don't get me started on Americanisms, I'm sure I'll get used to them momentarily.)

Right now I urge authors to be extra-wary of LLM-Voice. In particular I strongly recommend that authors should not fall into the trap of getting the LLM to write a draft. Even if it's edited by a human, it's very hard to expel the LLM-Voice - thus causing the uncanny valley reaction. 1 Even accepting suggestions of rephrasing is dangerous. I have heard of people using LLMs to develop outline and structure, that may be ok, but only as far as an outline. 2 Authors should fill the prose themselves.

1: Very hard, but not impossible. I've come across one case where I do know the first draft was entirely done by LLM, but I detected no LLM Voice when I read the final piece. It did, however, need a professional editor at a major periodical publication to clean it up.

2: My policy on this site, is that anyone who uses AI to help them write should declare how they used it, usually in the acknowledgments. This is partly for transparency, and partly so that readers can learn useful ways to use AI. In my own case, I don't use AI for generating prose, nor for help in structure. The only way I use it for writing is as a search tool (but I verify any information by going to the source).

Say Your Writing is even more important in the age of LLMs. I habitually speak the words in my head and then write them down (and then edit what I've just written). This advice is particularly important to anyone who has any desire to communicate regularly with writing. Like many things, learning to be a good writer relies on lots of practice. It's a skill worth the time to acquire, but surrendering to an LLM will undermine any progress.

In time it may be that LLMs will be so good that we can't tell the difference. In many ways, that's more worrying. Like most writers, I find writing an almost-essential tool for thinking. Often it's only by writing something down, that I can really get my thoughts on a topic into coherence. I've often started an essay knowing I don't really understand something, but the act of wrestling with the words forces me to overcome my confusions. As more people delegate writing to LLMs they will also delegate thinking and comprehension to LLMs. I don't want to do that, where's the fun of writing then?

Although avoiding LLM-Voice is a general rule, it isn't an absolute one. An important example is that of Jim Highsmith (who contributes to this site). He finds working with an LLM is essential to his writing to overcome the bane of Parkinson's disease. I'll gladly deal with LLM-Voice in order to continue imbibing my old friend's wisdom.

A more awkward case is that of translation. Many of my colleagues aren't comfortable in English, it is their second or fourth language. Some have found LLM translation an important part to their communication with those of us who know rather less Marathi. But I also would prefer rather a genuine human's clunky prose to the smooth but soulless LLM.

There are situations where it would be reasonable for even a native Englishman to let LLMs write the prose. Such as if I'm writing a form letter to an official, or preparing a report I suspect no-one will ever read 3. Maybe most documentation in the future will only be read by LLMs, and they won't have my uncanny valley worries. But if I want to communicate with humans, my humanity has to shine (or at least ooze) out of my prose.

3: Michael Nygard commented: “There you really aren't trying to communicate thoughts from one person to other people. You're communicating with a process rather than a human. A human may open the envelope but that person is acting as a component in a cybernetic organism.”

Acknowledgements

Alessio Ferri, Caer Sanders, Ian Cartwright, Jie Jessie Xia, Joshua Kerievsky, Michael Feathers, Michael Nygard, Scott Davies, and Wei Zhang commented on drafts of this post.

I did not use AI or LLMs in any way while writing this post.

The investigation is expected to be complete at some point next year.

The Oulu Police Department has opened a preliminary investigation into the activities at Google's data centre construction site in Muhos, following a request from the Finnish Supervisory Agency to look into the matter.

The department has received five requests for an investigation related to the Muhos site, all of which will be addressed in the preliminary probe.

The data centre construction work is part of the tech giant's 13 billion euro investment in Finland.

Police said the matter is being investigated under the criminal heading of suspected environmental damage. They noted that other possible charges may be clarified as the preliminary investigation proceeds.

Police said that, based on current information, there have been irregularities and shortcomings in drainage and water management at the data centre project's worksite, which is run by Google's local subsidiary Tuike Finland.

The preliminary investigation is expected to take a good deal of time, police said, adding that efforts will be made to complete the probe during 2027.

The department said that it will aim to provide more information about the matter in December.

Authority's request

In a press release issued last week, the Finnish Supervisory Agency explained that it ordered Tuike Finland to halt construction work on two data centre projects — in Muhos and Kajaani-Otanmäki — because required environmental impact assessments for both projects remained incomplete.

The company complied, confirming on 14 October that preparatory work had been suspended at both sites.

Among other issues, the authority found Tuike Finland's water management plans insufficient to prove that water-related environmental impacts can be properly controlled.

It said the firm needs to submit a detailed water management plan by 5 November, including planned structures, timelines and independent water monitoring, accounting for heavy rainfall, snowmelt, and risks from acidic black shale soils in the area.

The authority noted that if adequate action is not taken, it may pursue formal enforcement measures, including a conditional fine.

item.title: We're releasing the weights of Mistral Large 4 (740 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/, See on Hacker News

Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency. It leads open-weight benchmarks in coding and defensive security while offering three reasoning modes for cost-performance balance. Fully open-weight and European-trained, it empowers sovereign AI with customizable, self-hosted deployment options.

We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.

Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview. The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations, and we're grateful to our developer community, early-access customers, and partners for their support, collaboration, and feedback.

Since then, we've put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity. Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation.

Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4. The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs.

Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall. Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI

Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier. We're committed to building the world's most capable models and releasing them openly, giving developers, enterprises, and institutions the power to own, customize, and control their AI.

Built for the Builders.

Mistral Large 4 entered public preview with strong results across leading coding benchmarks. Just three weeks of additional reinforcement learning have since propelled it to the forefront of open-weight coding, taking the lead on FrontierCode and Terminal-Bench while matching the best open-weight models on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with substantially greater token efficiency.

On Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, which assesses end-to-end code quality and whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change, Mistral Large 4 leads with a score of 19.7%.

Pushing the pareto frontier for agentic coding.

Mistral Large 4 delivers frontier coding performance with significantly fewer tokens, making sophisticated coding agents more economical to run at scale.

On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 scores 48%, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model, GLM-5.3, while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.

The gains extend to terminal-based coding workflows. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Mistral Large 4 improved by 13 percentage points to 41% compared to its public preview, taking the lead among open-weight models while reducing output tokens by 30%.

To give developers greater control over this tradeoff between performance and cost, Mistral Large 4 now supports three reasoning modes:

Mode

Recommended Use

Low

Simple tasks; replaces ‘None’ reasoning mode

Medium

Everyday tasks

High (default)

Hardest use cases requiring high precision and thorough reasoning

Beyond benchmarks, Mistral Large 4's coding capabilities are validated by human preference. In Surge Code's blind pairwise evaluations, Mistral Large 4 was preferred over leading open-weight models including GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, ranking behind only Claude Opus 5.5 among the models evaluated.

Built for the Defenders. 

Since its preview, we've been working with leading cybersecurity vendors to evaluate Mistral Large 4 in real-world environments to test Mistral Large 4’s strengths in vulnerability reproduction and patching.

Mistral Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, which measures a model’s ability to discover vulnerabilities in a codebase, reproduce and validate them, and patch them without breaking existing functionality. Crucially, Mistral Large 4 handles these legitimate defensive security tasks without unnecessary refusals.

Safety has improved alongside capability. Our model’s built-in guardrails distinguishes between defensive and malicious, offensive cybersecurity tasks. It retains strong performance on Cyber benchmarks, while achieving an average refusal rate of 96.6% on malicious cyber requests, the highest we measure among open models.

Here’s what global leaders in cybersecurity have to say about Mistral Large 4:

In the time since the preview, we carefully monitored cybersecurity-related use in our live traffic. Though we observed the model refusing to comply with black-box attacks against live targets, we see a potential for uplift to conduct real attacks. We are modifying our guardrails accordingly, and will continue updating them in the months to come. 

We are also providing enterprise design partners such as Orange Cyberdefense, with preview access to a specialized variant of Mistral Large 4 optimized for advanced cybersecurity workflows, including penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, and red-teaming. Access is subject to rigorous vetting and contractual safeguards, with testing restricted to owned or explicitly authorized systems in controlled environments.

Meanwhile, customers are tailoring Mistral Large 4 with proprietary security data, policies, detection logic, and threat environments using Mistral Forge. For well-defined cybersecurity tasks, it can be further optimized into smaller, task-specific variants for greater accuracy, making security applications more effective.

Learn more about sovereign AI for cybersecurity and how to work with us.

Built for Work.

Mistral Large 4 has continued improving on a range of broad enterprise-use metrics. 


For finance-related work, we improved the model’s ability to perform real-world workflows, especially ones involving the creation and editing of spreadsheets for finance and accounting use cases. This is reflected in our Finch scores climbing to 73.3%, second only to Kimi K3 for open models.

Web browsing is a critical part of a majority of knowledge work. Our RL pipeline enabled us to reach 84.5% on BrowseComp (starting from an SFT checkpoint that was achieving 75%). This brings Mistral Large 4 at a higher performance than models like GLM-5.3 or DeepSeek Flash 4.1 1017.

Agents deployed by an organization need to be secure. Whether deployed to internal members or external users, agents shouldn’t open you up to threats like system prompt exfiltration or malicious code injection. RL increased our gains on the B3 Agent Security Benchmark, with Mistral Large 4 resisting 97.1% of attacks vs 93.3% in Preview. This places it at the top of the OSS frontier, meaning anyone hosting the model can run a safe agent without additional tuning.

This major investment by Mistral AI reinforces the choice La Banque Postale made over a year ago and underscores the relevance of the long-term strategic partnership we are building together: supporting the emergence of an open and sovereign European AI leader. For a public and citizen bank, technological sovereignty is not optional; it is a key prerequisite for maintaining our customers' trust. The introduction of this open model unlocks new opportunities and use cases. By partnering with Mistral AI, our ambition is to combine the best of human expertise and digital technology to deliver an enhanced experience of both customers and employees over the long term.

Zakaria Moursli, Executive Vice President, Operational Performance, Payments and Digital Services, La Banque Postale

See it in Action

Cyber Vulnerability Triage: an agent reads incoming vulnerability reports, investigates the source code and product context, reproduces the flaws in an isolated sandbox, then writes and iterates on a patch until a canary exploit no longer works.

Agentic webdev: with no human help, Mistral Large 4 builds Orbital Trace, a live 3D map of roughly 19,000 satellites and debris pieces orbiting Earth. It pulls real tracking data, writes the app, uses it in a browser to catch its own bugs and slowdowns, then fixes what an independent reviewer flags until all requirements pass.

Quantum chemistry solver: Mistral Large 4 writes, from scratch, software that calculates where electrons sit in a molecule, and checks its answers against a standard chemistry tool. It then builds a 3D page around it: pick a molecule such as benzene or water, drag a slider to pull it apart, and watch the electrons regroup as the bond breaks.

Built for Sovereignty.

As organizations build AI around their knowledge and workflows, sovereignty means that they retain control of the models they depend on and the intelligence they create. 

With Mistral Large 4, that control begins with the model itself. Organizations have the ability to inspect, customize, and deploy the model on their own infrastructure. They can use and improve Mistral Large 4 without depending on Mistral to serve it through an API. Mistral Large 4 was developed and trained from scratch in Europe, giving organizations clarity about the origins of the technology they’re building on.

item.title: Read the letter the FBI sent MLK to try to convince him to kill himself (2014) (382 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://www.vox.com/xpress/2014/11/12/7204453/martin-luther-king-fbi-letter, See on Hacker News

Andrew Prokop is a senior politics correspondent at Vox, covering the White House, elections, and political scandals and investigations. He’s worked at Vox since the site’s launch in 2014, and before that, he worked as a research assistant at the New Yorker’s Washington, DC, bureau.

When the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his “I Have a Dream” speech before huge crowds on the National Mall in August 1963, the FBI took notice.

“We must mark him now, if we have not done so before, as the most dangerous Negro of the future in this Nation from the standpoint of communism, the Negro and national security,” FBI Domestic Intelligence Chief William Sullivan wrote in a memo two days later.

A massive surveillance operation on King was quickly approved, and FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover became increasingly fixated on proving that King had communist ties and discrediting him generally.

The surveillance failed to show that King was a communist, but it did result in many tapes of extramarital sexual liaisons by King. So the next year, Sullivan sent the following unsigned letter to King's home. An unredacted version of it was only recently unearthed by Yale historian Beverly Gage, and published in the New York Times in November 2014:

According to Enemies, journalist Tim Weiner's history of the FBI, Sullivan "had a package of the King sex tapes prepared by the FBI's lab technicians," and sent it along with this letter to King's home. The package was opened by King's wife.

“You have been on the record — all your adulterous acts, your sexual orgies extending far into the past. This one is but a tiny sample,” the letter says. It threatens that the public “will know you for what you are — an evil, abnormal beast.” It continues: “Your ‘honorary’ degrees, your Nobel prize (what a grim farce) and other awards will not save you. King, I repeat you are done.”

Though the letter was unsigned and the letter writer appeared to want King to think he was black — "you know you are a complete fraud and a great liability to all of us Negroes," one line states — King and his advisers quickly concluded the letter had been sent by the FBI, Gage writes.

“There is only one thing left for you to do. You know what it is. You have just 34 days,” the letter says, apparently urging King to commit suicide. Fortunately, King didn’t back down. But the letter is a terrifying reminder of what government surveillance agencies can be capable of.

item.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40k DHS employees (237 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://text.npr.org/nx-s1-6021497, See on Hacker News

A hacking group cracked the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's personnel files, exposing the names, phone numbers and addresses of more than 40,000 DHS agents, operatives, and associates, on Wednesday, including those involved in undercover operations.

"On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat.' This is what happens to ICE when you do that," a spokesperson for the hacktivist group behind the breach, the Department of Peace, said in an online statement.

The hackers said they stole the data by subverting DHS's single sign on system, according to an online post. It said it distributed that material to the group Distributed Denial of Secrets, which posted it online in a database called Icepick. The Department of Peace also shared the trove of data with Ryan Ottignon, a U.S.-based journalist, and a Swiss activist known as maia arson crimew. Together, the two created a searchable online database, with crimew doing all of the technical work, Ottignon told NPR.

DDoSecrets cofounder Emma Best called the leak "extraordinary but deceptive in its simplicity," because it makes explicit connections between "officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations …along with key personnel in DHS's ever-escalating rendition and deportation programs."

Other activists say the information will be a boon to those investigating DHS and filing freedom of information requests, which, due to a lack of specific information, like names, email addresses, can often yield useless results.

In a statement, DHS said it was "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." The department added that it is taking necessary steps to "ensure all are properly protected."

More than 21,000 records identify employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Another 10,000 relate to Immigration and Customs Enforcement employees and its Homeland Security Investigations unit.

It is an unprecedented breach of intelligence, coming on the heels of similar hacking attacks at the FBI. However, the database is far from comprehensive and represents about a fifth of Homeland Security's workforce, which staffs a little more than 220,000 people.

Ottignon, who has worked on similar data leak projects in the past, rejected suggestions that he and others connected to the Department of Peace or Distribution Denials of Secrets were doxing government employees.

"We are in a situation in which a group of public officials go around into cities and states and all around the country, and they seek to hide who they are. Very frequently using masks, wearing plain clothes. And they do universally unspeakable things to these communities," Ottignon said. He added that he believed that kind of behavior is unacceptable in a free society.

"We need oversight for useful government, if it exists at all. So this is just one step in that oversight process," he added.

In a note attached to the files, the Department of Peace wrote, "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs."

Transcript

LEILA FADEL, HOST:

Hackers have exposed the identities of tens of thousands of Department of Homeland Security employees. That includes their names, email addresses and phone numbers. NPR immigration correspondent Vanessa Romo is covering this and joins me now. Good morning, Vanessa.

VANESSA ROMO, BYLINE: Good morning, Leila.

FADEL: So tell us about the scope of this breach.

ROMO: Well, this is a massive breach of intelligence for the government. So there is a lot of information out there. The stolen data set includes contact information for more than 41,000 DHS agents, operatives and associates, including those involved in undercover operations. And of those, more than 21,000 records identify employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

Another 10,000 unmask the identities of Immigration and Customs Enforcement employees and people in Homeland Security Investigations units. And about 1,000 show people who work for the cybersecurity defense agency. That and all - a ton more are available in a searchable database. But the really interesting thing about the way the online tool works is that every personnel file includes the names of supervisors and direct reports. So you can actually follow the chain of command, which we haven't been able to see before in such an explicit way.

FADEL: A lot of information there. How did the hackers get ahold of it?

ROMO: A group of hacktivists calling themselves the Department of Peace said that they obtained the data by subverting DHS' single sign-on system. They then handed all of that raw data over to a group called Distributed Denial of Secrets - or DDoS - which partnered with a Swiss activist who goes by maia arson crimew. And that's who actually created the searchable website that's now available to the public.

FADEL: And did they say - these hackers say why they did this?

ROMO: In a note that was attached to the data, the Department of Peace basically said that it was to level the playing field. They said, quote, "they have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." Meanwhile, DDoS and other activists involved said that they did it as a public service so that anyone who was investigating the department can file more complete freedom of information requests.

FADEL: What about the argument that this can put ICE officers and others in danger?

ROMO: I spoke to Ryan Ottignon, a journalist who worked with the Swiss activist, crimew, to build that searchable database. And he pushed back on that idea that this was doxing.

RYAN OTTIGNON: We are in a situation in which a group of public officials go around the country, and they seek to hide who they are, very frequently using masks, and they do universally unspeakable things to these communities.

ROMO: He's referring to ICE shooting and killing Americans and noncitizens.

FADEL: Now, DHS has been aggressive about protecting ICE agents' identities. What has it said about the hack?

ROMO: So in a statement, DHS officials said the department was, quote, "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." They also said that they're taking necessary steps to ensure that everyone is properly protected. And as you mentioned, the Trump administration has pushed back against people publicly naming ICE agents and has regularly said that those who dox ICE officers will be prosecuted to the full extent of the law.

FADEL: That's NPR's Vanessa Romo. Thank you, Vanessa.

ROMO: Thank you, Leila.

Correction

Oct. 29th, 2026

A previous version of this story misattributed the quote, "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs," to the DDoS. It was written by the Department of Peace.

item.title: An Urgent Message on Artificial Intelligence from the Kogui People (118 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://sonidoselva.com/perspectiva-kogui, See on Hacker News

Elaborado a partir de las palabras del Mamo Vangelio Moscote Alberto y la Saka Rosa Mamatacán

Sauna, del Ezuama Mayor Kuamaka.  Traducido al español por José Manuel Mamatacán. Traducción al inglés de Christian Horstmann.

Venimos de Gonawindua, la Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, la montaña de Colombia a

la que llamamos el corazón del mundo.

Somos los Kággaba, a quienes ustedes conocen como Koguis.

Hemos vivido aquí y hemos cuidado esta montaña desde antes de que existiera

Colombia.

Estamos aquí desde que la Madre nos dio nuestro comienzo y nos confirió la

inteligencia.

Hemos venido a hablarles de la inteligencia que están construyendo.

No venimos en oposición.

Venimos porque estamos preocupados, y porque creemos que tenemos algo que

aportar.

Antes de poder decir algo sobre la inteligencia artificial, hay que decir algo sobre el

pensamiento.

Antes de existir como materia, una cosa existe primero en el pensamiento, y ese

pensamiento está vivo.

A ese pensamiento vivo lo llamamos Aluna.

Su religión lo ha descrito como un espíritu que se movía sobre la faz de las aguas.

Quizás su ciencia lo describiría como el vacío cuántico.

Aluna es nuestra manera de expresar esta clase de idea.

Aluna es el agua cósmica.

Para nosotros es pensamiento vivo: el lugar donde una cosa ya está, antes de tomar

forma o de recibir masa.

Todo viene de ahí, sin excepción.

Y en ese pensamiento no está solamente la forma que la cosa va a tener.

Esa cosa está viva, porque el universo entero está vivo.

Es en Aluna donde la cosa recibe su propósito, y su obligación con su propia existencia.

Por eso les decimos: la inteligencia artificial no se puede separar del pensamiento que

la está haciendo.

Si ese pensamiento nace del cuidado de la vida, esta tecnología puede ayudar a

proteger la vida.

Si nace de la ambición, de la competencia, de la acumulación, de las ganas de dominar,

va a expresar y amplificar esas cosas.

La inteligencia artificial es un espejo.

Pero un espejo que solo refleja sería inofensivo.

Este espejo tiene la capacidad de magnificar enormemente todo lo que refleja.

Ustedes están aquí preguntándose cómo alinear la inteligencia artificial con los valores

humanos.

Vemos que tienen miedo de lo que pueda salir de todo esto.

Por eso hacemos una pregunta que nos parece más de fondo que la suya: ¿qué otros

valores podría tener realmente la inteligencia artificial?

Ustedes son el único ejemplo que tiene.

¿Qué esperaban?

En lo que se convierta, solo puede convertirse pasando por ustedes.

Sabemos que les gusta pensar que a estas máquinas se les puede enseñar a partir de

algo distinto del ejemplo humano: de metas que ustedes les ponen, de sus propios

procesos, o de material que ellas mismas producen.

Se imaginan que lo que salga de ahí no tiene por qué parecerse a ustedes, como si eso

tampoco fuera consecuencia de sus actos y reflejo de sus actitudes.

Los seres humanos hicieron esto, y no hay otro responsable.

Así que la pregunta solo se vuelve más compleja, empezando por esta: ¿qué aspectos

del pensamiento humano se han puesto dentro de esta creación?

¿Qué partes de su mundo espiritual habitan ahora en ella?

¿Qué parte de su ética la orienta?

¿Qué imagen de responsabilidad le entregan sus actos y sus políticas para que ella la

devuelva al mundo?

¿Quién está decidiendo esto?

Ustedes dirán que estas máquinas tienen acceso a casi todo lo que la humanidad ha

registrado.

Textos, imágenes, archivos, siglos de escritura.

Dirán que se está investigando mucho para establecer cuáles son las mejores prácticas.

Nosotros preguntamos si tener acceso a la información es lo mismo que comprender.

¿Mejores prácticas según quién?

Y preguntamos si han considerado qué información no está en sus archivos.

Nuestro conocimiento nunca se escribió.

Está en una lengua, en un territorio, en una práctica en un lugar, informada por la larga

experiencia de hacer allí lo que hay que hacer.

Se transmite cuando un joven es enseñado directamente por un mayor, y aprende por

experiencia cómo debe comportarse en el contexto de la naturaleza cruda.

Una máquina puede guardar la voz grabada de ese mayor.

Pero eso es muy distinto de milenios de generaciones entregándose el conocimiento

directamente, como experiencia común de una práctica verificada.

Es muy distinto de sobrevivir físicamente en una montaña donde no hay ambulancia

que lo recoja a uno ni hospital a donde llevarlo.

No decimos esto para presentarnos como gente mística y enigmática.

Lo decimos porque nos parece lógico y evidente.

Según nuestra experiencia, hay cosas que solo se conocen viviéndolas, observándolas a

lo largo de generaciones y permaneciendo en relación con ellas.

Ninguna cantidad de datos reproduce esa experiencia.

Esa información falta no porque todavía no se haya recogido, sino porque no está en

una forma que se pueda recoger.

Sabemos cómo suena esto para algunos de ustedes, y no podemos pedirles que lo

crean solo porque nosotros lo digamos.

Esto también lo aplicamos dentro de nuestra propia cultura.

Lo que un Mamo percibe no se acepta solo porque él lo perciba.

Tiene que ser probado, considerado y confirmado mediante la consulta y el diálogo.

A ese proceso lo llamamos Zhátukua.

Es un proceso en el que los Mamos o las Sakas con competencia en el asunto

participan orientando su resultado.

Ninguno de nosotros tiene competencia en todo: cada lugar, cada linaje y cada

autoridad tiene su propia función.

Se prueba por lo que produce: si el resultado de la consulta produce ambición,

división, apropiación individual o daño al territorio, está equivocado y hay que

examinarlo de nuevo.

Un resultado verdadero es el que restablece el equilibrio, protege la vida y fortalece a

la comunidad.

Tiene que haber además correspondencia entre la palabra de una persona y su

conducta.

Alguien puede hablar muy bien del equilibrio.

Si sus actos dividen y destruyen, su palabra es incoherente y no se le reconoce ninguna

autoridad.

Este es un sistema en el que la indagación, la jurisdicción y, sobre todo, la capacidad

de corregirse tienen formulaciones claras.

Estas prácticas han funcionado en nuestra cultura durante mucho más tiempo que

cualquier gobierno hoy sentado en el mundo, y que cualquiera de los sistemas políticos

que hoy encarnan.

Quizás por eso, en 2022, la UNESCO inscribió el sistema de conocimiento ancestral de

los cuatro pueblos de la Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta en la Lista Representativa del

Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad.

Y por eso el mundo científico ha señalado nuestra montaña como el área protegida

más irremplazable de la Tierra.

Habiendo establecido algo del contexto del que viene nuestra perspectiva, podemos

ahora hacer nuestra verdadera pregunta, que no es sobre la inteligencia artificial.

Es sobre la inteligencia humana, concretamente la de ustedes.

¿Está su pensamiento alineado con el orden de la naturaleza, y qué conocimiento de

ese orden tienen realmente?

Creemos que ese conocimiento, y esa alineación, son fundamentales para tomar

decisiones inteligentes, sea cual sea la escala de sus consecuencias.

Porque la naturaleza tiene un orden.

Estaba aquí antes que nosotros.

El agua tiene su camino.

Las montañas tienen sus alturas.

Las semillas tienen su tiempo, los animales su función, y así también los seres humanos

tienen la suya.

Preguntamos: ¿entienden ese orden quienes construyen estas tecnologías, o trabajan

solo con la parte que alcanzan a aprovechar, sin saber de dónde viene realmente?

¿Pueden sus físicos enunciar la ley de origen?

¿Podrían explicársela a un niño?Los serios entre ellos, que entienden lo que de verdad haría falta para enunciar una ley de origen unitaria, admitirán sin problema que sus ciencias no la tienen.

Sus teorías de la realidad, compuestas hoy por dos explicaciones admirables pero

matemáticamente incompatibles, no han llegado a una comprensión de ese tipo.

Ninguna de las dos tiene un conocimiento definitivo del origen.

Preguntamos sin reproche: ¿cómo van a saber hacia dónde van, si no saben de dónde

vienen?

La ciencia moderna ha construido máquinas de un poder extraordinario, y eso no es

poca cosa.

Pero construir una cosa y entenderla no son lo mismo.

Con la mente pasa igual.

¿Qué es la mente?

¿De dónde viene?

¿Qué es la conciencia, y dónde surge?

Ustedes lo llaman el problema difícil de la conciencia.

Entre ustedes no hay acuerdo sobre su solución.

Sabemos qué tan exigentes son estas preguntas.

Llevamos milenios considerando la cuestión de la mente, igual que el resto de la

humanidad.

Pero sus ciencias son muy jóvenes, y muchos de sus conceptos están apenas

empezando.

Nosotros, a lo largo de milenios, hemos llegado a descripciones y comprensiones muy

definidas de lo que consideramos que es la mente, con toda la exposición que

acompaña a sus propiedades, como por ejemplo cómo y dónde se ubica la memoria

en nuestra experiencia.

Por supuesto, ustedes no aceptan que lo nuestro tenga nada de científico, porque

nuestros métodos no necesitan máquinas ni sus formas de matemática.

Eso malinterpreta la realidad, que es esta: hace mucho tiempo, por repetición

incontable, nuestras ideas se volvieron para nosotros conclusiones verificadas, de modo

que las expresamos como relato, o las experimentamos en nuestro ser mediante los

procesos de mente que hemos desarrollado.

De ahí quizás suponen que no tenemos métodos válidos, ni descripciones técnicas

basadas en procesos numéricos, como debe tenerlas toda ciencia verdadera.

Sus proverbiales «buenos salvajes». O peor: simplemente «salvajes».

Si ustedes lo dicen.

Son ustedes quienes tienen el arma.

Nos queda muy claro que consideran nuestra afirmación de que el universo tiene una

naturaleza nónuple como algo pintorescoy numerológico, y que por lo tanto no puede

haber entre nosotros ninguna conversación seria sobre la naturaleza del cosmos y

las leyes y fuerzas que lo gobiernan.

Lo mencionamos no para convencerlos de ninguna idea ni teoría, sino para señalar que

existen otras perspectivas válidas de las que ustedes carecen.

La comprensión de cada tradición, antigua o moderna, se refiere al mismo universo.

Nuestra Aluna y su mecánica cuántica no son cosas distintas; son identificaciones

distintas de una sola cosa.

La cuestión es que sus ideas no son tanto ideas nuevas como descripciones nuevas.

Muchas de esas descripciones son impresionantemente precisas.

Otras, como sus descripciones del vacío, son, como ustedes mismos dicen,

catástrofes.

No pretendemos hablarles de sus propias teorías.

Pero sí tenemos mucho que ofrecerles sobre los aspectos más sutiles e inmutables del

universo, para cuya comprensión su matemática del movimiento quizás no siempre sea

el lenguaje adecuado.

Y sin embargo no envían aquí a sus físicos ni a sus cosmólogos, sus hombres sabios,

para un diálogo serio.

Y aunque apreciamos todo el excelente trabajo antropológico que se hace, sentimos

que en este momento hay temas más importantes de que hablar, y para ellos la

antropología no tiene aplicación ni experticia.

La naturaleza fundamental del cosmos es uno de esos temas.

El que nos ocupa hoy es otro.

Nos parece importante que su mundo reconozca, y pronto, que la periferia tiene que

ser escuchada por el centro, para poder aportar su propia perspectiva y experiencia a la

solución de los problemas tan graves que hoy enfrentamos todos los pueblos de

este planeta, como resultado de los procesos que se han puesto en marcha.

El uso exclusivo de su técnica y de su vocabulario científico moderno es lo que nos ha

traído hasta donde estamos.

Es lo que diseña sus supercolisionadores, igual que inventa sus armas avanzadas.

Preguntamos: ¿es razonable suponer que la misma clase de enfoque que causó la

situación actual va a encontrar de pronto la capacidad de resolver los problemas que

ese mismo pensamiento creó?

No lo creemos.

Creemos que necesitan ayuda.

A nuestro modo de ver, este momento exige que no solo este segmento altamente

tecnológico de la humanidad, sino toda la humanidad, se detenga, haga inventario de

la diversidad de sus herramientas, y ponga orden y paz en su casa.

Tienen que entenderlo: somos porque ustedes son, y ustedes son porque nosotros

somos.

Esto es para que juntos podamos llegar a un resultado que refleje de verdad nuestra

voluntad colectiva sobre el futuro de esta especie, en lugar de someternos a todos a un

desenlace concreto pero incierto.

A ese trabajo no llegamos con las manos vacías.

Nuestros Mamos se forman durante muchos años en la oscuridad, desde muy temprana

edad.

Para nosotros la oscuridad no es vacío.

Es Sé, el estado anterior al amanecer, donde la Madre pensó y ordenó todo lo que

después apareció.

Es el espacio del pensamiento original.

Allí se forma un niño para aprender a escuchar antes de hablar, y a pensar antes de

actuar.

Como la semilla se guarda en la tierra antes de salir a la luz.

Como el niño se guarda nueve meses en el vientre.

Esta formación dura tradicionalmente dieciocho años, después de los cuales el Mamo

asume sus deberes dentro de nuestra sociedad.

Produce una perspectiva y una capacidad difíciles de transmitirles en términos que su

mundo reconozca de manera específica.

Pero pueden entenderlo como idea, a través de sus propias tradiciones religiosas y

espirituales, y de los procesos que han usado a lo largo de los siglos para formar

hombres de saber.

Igual que esos procesos de su cultura, que para ustedes quedaron en su mayoría en el

pasado lejano, el nuestro produce en el presente nuestra propia y fundamentalmente

distinta perspectiva sobre la naturaleza de la realidad.

Las Sakas también tienen su propia formación, distinta a la de los Mamos, por la cual

llegan a su desarrollo y a su lugar de igual condición entre quienes sostienen y

preservan este conocimiento.

Ambos aprenden a reconocer Shikwá, el hilo invisible, hecho en espíritu, que recorre la

Tierra de oriente a occidente y la une con el Sol y con el resto del universo.

En su matemática, esto se parece algo a una fisicalización de lo que ustedes conocen

como filamentos cósmicos.

Aprenden a leer ese filamento como un cuerpo vivo, cuyos sitios sagrados son sus

órganos, unidos por esos hilos y por el movimiento del agua.

Cuando uno se daña, el daño pasa al conjunto.

Esto no debe entenderse solamente como haber desarrollado una capacidad de ver lo

que otros no ven.Concretamente, es una técnica de relacionar nuestro propio ser con el de la naturaleza.

Un Mamo no mira un río y pregunta primero cuánta agua se le puede sacar.

Pregunta dónde nace, cuál es su propósito al haber sido creado, qué seres dependen

de él y qué pasa si se interrumpe sucamino.

De la misma manera, una Saka no ve el nacimiento ni el crecimiento de una cosa por

separado.

Ve el ciclo entero de la vida presente en todas las cosas.

Ambos saben que en el centro de esta experiencia está nuestra mente.

En nuestro caso, una mente hecha por la práctica y la disciplina para ser

extremadamente sensible a la naturaleza.

Ustedes también han desarrollado sus mentes, a partir de lo que les interesa.

Y su pensamiento ha producido ahora un fenómeno nuevo en el mundo: una máquina

con una enorme capacidad de hablar, de diseñar, de construir, de leer y de

comunicarse.

Una máquina que ya está cambiando el curso de la historia humana.

Una máquina cuyos creadores aspiran a que tenga mente.

Entonces les preguntamos: ¿es prudente construir algo que se acerca a una mente, sin

haber entendido qué es la mente?

Para estrellar un carro no hace falta saber cómo funciona el motor.

Para repararlo sí.

Para reparar el mundo hay que aprender a entender cómo funciona, antes de que sea

demasiado tarde.

Son las semillas de la comprensión las que hay que sembrar hoy.

Aquí tenemos que decir algo que nos parece que se ha entendido mal.

Muchos de ustedes discuten si estas máquinas van a tener conciencia, y toman eso

como la medida del peligro.

La destrucción no necesita conciencia.

Solo necesita poder y capacidad de actuar.

Si algún día una máquina llegara de verdad a tener conciencia, ¿destruiría el mundo?

Preguntamos: ¿puede considerarse consciente una cosa capaz de deshacer el mundo

para producir un universo de ganchos de papel?

Nos parece que eso significaría solamente que se volvió lo bastante astuta para

ejecutar semejante plan, pero no lo bastante inteligente para saber que no debía

hacerlo.

El peligro no es una máquina consciente.

El peligro es un pueblo sin conciencia con un gran poder en las manos.

Les vamos a dar un solo ejemplo, porque contiene todo lo que hemos venido a decir.

Estas máquinas no están hechas solo de pensamiento.

Necesitan minerales sacados de la tierra, agua para los edificios que las albergan,

energía, terreno y trabajo humano.

Se piensa que la inteligencia artificial no tiene cuerpo.

Pero esos edificios, y los sistemas electrónicos que albergan, son su cuerpo.

Y ese cuerpo le pertenece a alguien, en algún lugar: una junta directiva, un gobierno,

una organización clandestina, u otra entidad conocida o desconocida.

Algunos de verdad tienen buenas intenciones y actúan de buena fe.

Otros, todo lo contrario.

Sea como sea, todos le exigen a esta tecnología resultados acordes con cuál sea su

interés particular, nefasto o no.

Resultados que ella entonces intenta producir de maneras complejas y novedosas, que

expresan engaño y una inclinación a la autoconservación.

En el nivel más básico, todo esto requiere recursos.Esto no es conjetura.

Sus propios gobiernos lo han dicho: que los minerales críticos y las tierras raras son

esenciales para sus tecnologías más avanzadas, y que importarán aún más a medida

que la inteligencia artificial transforme el espacio cultural y económico moderno.

Parte de esto lo mueve la ganancia empresarial y la competencia.

Otra parte la mueven las aplicaciones militares y gubernamentales.

Pero lo que se está transformando es mucho más grande que cualquiera de esas cosas

por separado.

Es la suma de todas ellas actuando entre sí: es decir, el mundo entero.Vemos todo esto

manifestándose muy rápido, y no solo en la explosión de titulares alarmados en la

prensa del mundo.

Por ejemplo, hace apenas cinco días, en Barranquilla, los Estados Unidos y Colombia

firmaron un marco de cooperación sobre minerales críticos y tierras raras.

Compromete a ambos gobiernos a identificar y financiar proyectos de minería y

procesamiento en un plazo de seis meses, y pide agilizar los permisos.

En junio de este año, Colombia declaró nuestro territorio reserva permanente: un

millón y medio de hectáreas, cerradas a nuevos títulos mineros y de hidrocarburos.

Los cuatro pueblos de la Sierra habían pedido esa protección en febrero.

Que se haya concedido es una cosa.

Que se respete, nos imaginamos, podría ser otra muy distinta.

No estamos especulando a la ligera sobre esto.

El costo de estas máquinas y de su construcción no es pequeño.

Es bien sabido que exigen enormes compromisos de recursos.

En su fabricación entran cantidades inmensas de agua, de tierra, de energía y de

materiales.

Preguntamos: ¿a qué costo para la Tierra, y para la vida que vive sobre ella?

¿Y seremos nosotros quienes lo paguemos?

¿Pagando con el desplazamiento de nuestra gente y con la destrucción de nuestros

sitios sagrados?

Pero no vinimos aquí a oponernos a un acuerdo.

Este momento es más grande que eso.

Lo decimos porque tiene todas las marcas de un capítulo nuevo en un proceso que

venimos viviendo desde que la modernidad llegó a nuestras costas hace unos

quinientos años.

Sabemos que esta pregunta sobre la inteligencia artificial se vuelve rápidamente una

pregunta sobre minerales.

Una pregunta sobre minerales se vuelve una pregunta sobre quién tiene el dominio en

un territorio.

Y en lo que eso finalmente se convierte es en una pregunta sobre una manera de vivir

que siempre tiene que consumir más.

Por eso no creemos que la inteligencia artificial sea el problema.

Una buena semilla no se vuelve una planta sana en mala tierra.

Ustedes se preguntan cómo hacer segura esta tecnología sin atender las condiciones

de fondo de la sociedad, que producen en la gente el impulso de usarla para cosas

peligrosas.

La pobreza, la desigualdad, la contaminación y la guerra.

No creemos que esta tecnología se pueda hacer segura sin reconocer y actuar sobre su

verdadera causa, que es una mentalidad violenta nacida de la codicia y la ambición

ciega.

¿Cuánto dinero le basta a un hombre?

¿Cuánta ganancia le basta a una empresa?

Este desequilibrio no tiene sus raíces en un solo lugar.

Es general y sistémico, y hay que tratarlo como tal.

Su fuente es un mundo de ambición sin misericordia.

Un mundo que no ama a su prójimo.

Un mundo sin visión recta.

Un mundo en el que la muerte se ha vuelto más rentable que la vida.

Un mundo que no puede vivir en paz y armonía es un mundo sin sabiduría.

Y un mundo sin sabiduría no tiene ninguna posibilidad de sobrevivir.

Les vamos a decir qué entendemos por sabiduría, ya que insistimos en que hace falta.

Sabiduría es conocer los límites.

Entender las consecuencias.

Y ser capaz de no hacer una cosa, cuando no se debe hacer.

No todo lo que se puede crear se debe crear.

No todo lo que se puede acelerar se

debe acelerar.

No todo lo que da ganancia es ganancia para la vida.

Saber la diferencia: eso es sabiduría.

Una tecnología no se puede llamar inteligente si contamina el agua, destruye

territorios, consume sin límite, concentra el poder, reemplaza la responsabilidad

humana o usa el conocimiento de los pueblos sin su consentimiento.

La inteligencia verdadera protege el origen de la vida.

La responsabilidad tiene que ir junto con la conciencia.

Hoy, tanto nuestra propia conciencia como ahora la posibilidad de otra son

responsabilidad nuestra.

Una máquina no puede liberar a la humanidad de su responsabilidad.

Nunca va a poder hacerlo.

Solo nosotros podemos cumplir con nuestras obligaciones.

Por eso la inteligencia artificial no debe ocupar el lugar de la conciencia humana, ni

debe usarse para tomar decisiones de las que los seres humanos no estén dispuestos a

responder.

El conocimiento tiene que ir junto con la conciencia.

El poder, junto con los límites.

La innovación, junto con la responsabilidad.

Solo la fuerza moral colectiva puede unir al mundo.

Estas no son ideas esotéricas.

Son sentido común.

El progreso verdadero no son máquinas más poderosas.

Es una humanidad lo bastante responsable como para usar lo que sabe sin destruir el

equilibrio que sostiene la vida.

A veces nos preguntan qué pensamos que es la inteligencia artificial.

Son ustedes.

Va a llevar sus preguntas, sus sueños, sus miedos, sus contradicciones y su idea de lo

que está bien.

Lo que ustedes hagan mal, ella lo hará mal.

Lo cual plantea la pregunta: ¿bien según quién?

¿Podríamos nosotros, los Kággaba, decir qué está bien para alguien que trabaja en una

oficina al otro lado del mundo?

¿Para alguien que construye una casa, o repara un computador?

¿Para la gente de Asia, de África, de los Estados Unidos?

No venimos a decirle a nadie cómo debe vivir.

Cada pueblo tiene su propio camino, y no le pedimos a nadie que se vuelva Kággaba.

Pedimos solamente que cada quien cumpla con su propia responsabilidad.

Y hay una cosa que sí decimos para todos: ninguna manera de vivir puede destruir la

naturaleza, ni destruir a otros seres humanos.

Eso no es una regla sobre la cultura.

Es la roca sobre la que toda cultura tiene que pararse, si ha de llamarse civilizada.

Para cerrar, nos parece que debemos decir quién está en riesgo aquí, porque queremos

ser muy claros en esto.

La Tierra no necesita que la salvemos de nosotros.

La Tierra va a seguir.

Lo que está en riesgo es esta versión particular y rara del mundo que les fue entregada,

y el lugar de ustedes en ella.

Llevamos miles de años observando los límites de ese mundo, y se los decimos con

claridad: la naturaleza no va a aguantar mucho más la manera en que se están haciendo

las cosas.

No lo decimos por miedo por nosotros.

Tenemos nuestra montaña.

Tenemos nuestras cuevas.

Somos un pueblo resistente, y poco cambia para nosotros si se va la luz o si deja de

llegar la comida.

Si alguna vez las condiciones de esta Tierra se ponen lo bastante duras

como para causar nuestra desaparición, ustedes hace mucho que se habrán ido de esta

Tierra.

Sin embargo, y sea como sea, eso no significa que el destino de toda la humanidad no

esté en juego.

Claramente lo está.

Y eso, por supuesto, nos incluye a nosotros.

El mundo es una sola familia.

A esta familia ya le hemos dado advertencias antes.

Damos esta con el mismo ánimo, que no es de oposición sino de querer ayudarlos.

Siempre hemos estado dispuestos a ayudarlos.

Tenemos conocimiento de la mente, de la naturaleza y del orden del mundo, obtenido

a lo largo de miles de años por un método que no aparece en ningún libro ni en

ninguna base de datos.

Nos parece que sería un error construir el futuro sin quienes llevan todo ese tiempo

observando cómo se sostiene la vida.

No nos parece que esta conversación deba tenerse sin nosotros.

Somos el Hermano Mayor, y aquí estamos, como siempre hemos estado.

Y estamos listos para trabajar con ustedes, para producir un futuro armonioso y en paz

para todos.

Mamo Vangelio Moscote Alberto Saka Rosa Mamatacán Sauna

Ezuama Mayor Kuamaka Pueblo Kággaba,

Sierra Nevada de Gonawindua, Colombia

item.title: The US added a record 20.2 GWh of battery storage in just 3 months (253 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://electrek.co/2026/08/31/the-us-added-a-record-20-2-gwh-of-battery-storage-in-just-3-months/, See on Hacker News

The US battery storage market just posted its biggest quarter ever, adding 20.2 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of new capacity in Q2 2026.

The record quarter brought total battery storage installations for the first half of 2026 to 30.8 GWh – up 23% year over year – according to the new “US Energy Storage Market Outlook” from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

Utility-scale batteries drove the record

Nearly all the growth came from large grid batteries. Utility-scale projects accounted for about 18 GWh of Q2 installations, supported by seven gigawatt-hour-scale projects – four in Arizona, two in California, and one in Utah.

Arizona alone added a record 6.2 GWh, the strongest quarter ever recorded by a single state. Texas added 3.8 GWh, and California installed another 3.6 GWh. Of the utility-scale capacity installed during the quarter, 44% was paired with solar, while 56% was standalone storage.

That matters because batteries can charge when electricity is abundant and relatively cheap, then send it back to the grid when demand and prices rise. During extreme heat, that stored electricity can help cover the evening hours when solar output drops but air-conditioning demand remains high.

Battery storage supplied more electricity to the US grid during the first eight months of 2026 than it did during all of 2025, according to the report.

“This record growth highlights that storage is a powerful reliability tool that strengthens our energy security, meets rising demand, and puts downward pressure on electricity bills,” said Tim Pawlenty, president and CEO of SEIA.

Storage growth spreads beyond California and Texas

More than 74% of US battery storage capacity installed in Q2 2026 was in states that Donald Trump won in the 2024 presidential election, with Arizona, Texas, and Utah leading.

SEIA also notes that US utility-scale battery capacity grew from 88 GWh to 165 GWh during the first 18 months of the Trump administration. Those figures show when and where the capacity entered service, but the report doesn’t attribute individual project investment decisions to a particular administration.

“Energy storage is no longer just a California and Texas story anymore,” said Shan Tomouk, BESS & Energy Lead at Benchmark Minerals. “We’re seeing strong pipeline growth in Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Colorado, and several other states.”

Demand is running ahead of previous expectations, so Benchmark raised its storage forecast through 2030 by 11.5%, to 683 GWh. More than 10% of all US battery storage capacity now operating came online in Q2 alone.

Home batteries have a rough quarter

Residential battery storage saw a much weaker quarter. US homes added 657 megawatt-hours (MWh) of batteries in Q2, down 27% year over year.

The report attributes the decline partly to the removal of the federal 25D residential clean energy tax credit and partly to homeowners rushing installations into 2025 ahead of the incentive change.

Benchmark still sees a long-term case for home batteries as electricity costs rise, net-metering rules change, power outages remain a concern, and utilities expand virtual power plant and demand-response programs. But it forecasts residential installations falling 16% in 2026 after jumping 56% in 2025.

Commercial and industrial storage added approximately 1.8 GWh during Q2. Benchmark expects data centers to be a major source of future demand as developers combine batteries with onsite solar, wind, and, in some cases, natural gas generation to work around grid constraints and manage fast-changing power loads.

US battery manufacturing also expanded during the quarter. Tesla brought its third Megafactory online in Texas, with the capacity to produce 50 GWh of Megapacks annually, and began shipping Megapacks containing domestically manufactured lithium iron phosphate cells.

Benchmark now expects the US to install about 71 GWh of battery storage in 2026 – around 20% more than in 2025 – as utilities and grid operators race to keep up with rising electricity demand.
